content: Rifampin has minimal potential to induce CYP3A4 enzyme activity, but its use can significantly impact the metabolism of various drugs by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme activity, particularly CYP3A4. Below are the detailed effects of rifampin on specific drugs and recommendations for clinical management: 1. Bazedoxifene/Conjugated Estrogens: Rifampin reduces the levels and efficacy of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by increasing their metabolism via CYP3A4. This reduction in exposure may increase the risk of endometrial hyperplasia. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 2. BCG Vaccine (Live): Rifampin decreases the efficacy of the BCG vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Coadministration is contraindicated. 3. Bedaquiline: Rifampin reduces bedaquiline levels by enhancing its metabolism via CYP3A4, potentially decreasing its therapeutic effect. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers or use alternative drugs. 4. Bosutinib: Rifampin decreases bosutinib plasma concentrations by approximately 85% through CYP3A4 induction. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 5. Brigatinib: Rifampin reduces brigatinib levels and efficacy by increasing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 6. Budesonide: Rifampin decreases budesonide levels by enhancing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 7. Buspirone: Rifampin reduces buspirone levels and efficacy by increasing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 8. Cabozantinib: Rifampin decreases cabozantinib levels by enhancing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. If unavoidable, increase the cabozantinib dose (40 mg/day for Cometriq or 20 mg/day for Cabometyx) and resume the previous dose 2–3 days after discontinuing the inducer. 9. Capivasertib: Rifampin reduces capivasertib exposure by inducing CYP3A4, potentially reducing its efficacy. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 10. Capmatinib: Rifampin decreases capmatinib levels by enhancing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 11. Carbamazepine: Rifampin reduces carbamazepine levels by increasing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 12. Ceftobiprole Medocaril Sodium: Ceftobiprole may increase rifampin levels by inhibiting OATP1B1/1B3 transporters. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 13. Ceritinib: Rifampin reduces ceritinib levels by enhancing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 14. Cilostazol: Rifampin decreases cilostazol levels and efficacy by increasing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 15. Cinacalcet: Rifampin reduces cinacalcet levels by enhancing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 16. Clopidogrel: Rifampin increases the metabolism of clopidogrel to its active metabolite via CYP3A4 induction. Monitor for increased antiplatelet effects when coadministered. 17. Clozapine: Rifampin reduces clozapine levels by increasing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 18. Colchicine: Rifampin decreases colchicine levels by enhancing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 19. Conivaptan: Rifampin reduces conivaptan levels by increasing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 20. Conjugated Estrogens (Oral and Vaginal): Rifampin decreases the levels and efficacy of conjugated estrogens by enhancing their metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 21. Copanlisib: Rifampin reduces copanlisib levels by enhancing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 22. Cortisone: Rifampin decreases cortisone levels by increasing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 23. Dabigatran: Rifampin reduces dabigatran levels by inducing P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporters. Avoid coadministration. 24. Dabrafenib: Rifampin decreases dabrafenib levels by enhancing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 25. Daridorexant: Rifampin reduces daridorexant levels by increasing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 26. Darifenacin: Rifampin decreases darifenacin levels by enhancing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 27. Darolutamide: Rifampin reduces darolutamide levels by inducing P-gp and CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration with combined P-gp and CYP3A4 inducers. 28. Darunavir: Rifampin reduces darunavir levels by enhancing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Coadministration is contraindicated. 29. Dasatinib: Rifampin decreases dasatinib levels by increasing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 30. Deflazacort: Rifampin reduces deflazacort levels by enhancing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inducers. 31. Deuruxolitinib: Rifampin decreases deuruxolitinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C9. Avoid coadministration with strong or moderate CYP2C9 inducers. 32. Dexamethasone: Rifampin reduces dexamethasone levels by increasing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 33. Diazepam: Rifampin decreases diazepam levels by enhancing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 34. Dihydroergotamine (Oral and Intranasal): Rifampin reduces dihydroergotamine levels by increasing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 35. Diltiazem: Rifampin decreases diltiazem levels by enhancing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or adjust dosage with close monitoring. 36. Dronedarone: Rifampin reduces dronedarone levels by increasing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 37. Duloxetine: Rifampin decreases duloxetine levels by inducing CYP1A2. Coadministration is contraindicated. 38. Duvelisib: Rifampin reduces duvelisib levels by inducing CYP3A4, potentially reducing its efficacy. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 39. Edoxaban: Rifampin reduces edoxaban levels by inducing P-gp. Avoid coadministration with potent P-gp inducers. 40. Elacestrant: Rifampin decreases elacestrant levels by enhancing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 41. Eletiptan: Rifampin reduces eletiptan levels by increasing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 42. Eliglustat: Rifampin significantly decreases eliglustat exposure by inducing CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration. 43. Eluxadoline: Rifampin increases eluxadoline levels by decreasing its metabolism. Reduce eluxadoline dose to 75 mg PO BID if coadministered with OATP1B1 inhibitors. 44. Elvitegravir: Rifampin reduces elvitegravir levels by inducing CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration. 45. Enasidenib: Rifampin increases enasidenib levels by inhibiting OATP1B1/1B3. Avoid coadministration with sensitive substrates. 46. Encorafenib: Rifampin decreases encorafenib levels by enhancing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 47. Entrectinib: Rifampin reduces entrectinib levels by increasing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 48. Enzalutamide: Rifampin decreases enzalutamide levels by inducing CYP3A4. If unavoidable, increase enzalutamide dose from 160 mg/day to 240 mg/day. 49. Erdafitinib: Rifampin reduces erdafitinib levels by altering its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 50. Ergotamine: Rifampin decreases ergotamine levels by enhancing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 51. Erlotinib: Rifampin reduces erlotinib levels by increasing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 52. Erythromycin (Base, Ethylsuccinate, Lactobionate, Stearate): Rifampin decreases erythromycin levels by enhancing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 53. Estradiol: Rifampin reduces estradiol levels by increasing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 54. Estrogens (Conjugated Synthetic): Rifampin decreases synthetic conjugated estrogen levels by enhancing their metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 55. Estropipate: Rifampin reduces estropipate levels by increasing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 56. Ethinyl Estradiol: Rifampin decreases ethinyl estradiol levels, reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Use nonhormonal contraceptives instead. 57. Etonogestrel: Rifampin reduces etonogestrel levels by enhancing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 58. Etrasimod: Rifampin decreases etrasimod levels by inducing CYP3A4, CYP2C8, and CYP2C9. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 59. Etravirine: Rifampin reduces etravirine levels by increasing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 60. Everolimus: Rifampin decreases everolimus levels by inducing CYP3A4 and P-gp. Coadministration is contraindicated. 61. Fedratinib: Rifampin reduces fedratinib levels by inducing CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 62. Felbamate: Rifampin decreases felbamate levels by enhancing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 63. Felodipine: Rifampin reduces felodipine levels by increasing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 64. Fesoterodine: Rifampin decreases fesoterodine levels by enhancing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 65. Fexinidazole: Rifampin increases fexinidazole levels by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 66. Finerinone: Rifampin reduces finerinone levels by enhancing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 67. Fludrocortisone: Rifampin decreases fludrocortisone levels by increasing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 68. Fosamprenavir: Rifampin reduces fosamprenavir levels by enhancing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Coadministration is contraindicated. 69. Fosaprepitant: Rifampin decreases fosaprepitant levels by inducing CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs.
